recommendations.regimenLabel: Stop the agent + supportive care (cooling, fluids, benzodiazepines)
steps: STOP the offending agent immediately (serotonergic drug or antipsychotic).
Aggressive cooling and IV fluids; benzodiazepines for agitation/rigidity; ICU for severe cases.
Serotonin syndrome: consider cyproheptadine. NMS: consider dantrolene ± bromocriptine.
Monitor for and treat rhabdomyolysis, hyperthermia, renal failure and DIC.
Supportive care; avoid restraints worsening hyperthermia.

drugRefs.dose: 1–2 mg IV, repeat and titrate to effect
drugRefs.why: First-line supportive measure for agitation, rigidity and autonomic instability in both serotonin syndrome and NMS; helps lower temperature.

drugRefs.dose: titrated to volume status and urine output
drugRefs.why: Rehydration supports cooling and protects renal function against rhabdomyolysis.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Serotonin Syndrome and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
Boyer & Shannon — The Serotonin Syndrome (NEJM Review)
Sternbach and Hunter Criteria for Serotonin Toxicity

drugRefs.dose: 12 mg initially, then 2 mg every 2 h until response (max ~32 mg/day)
drugRefs.why: 5-HT2A antagonist considered in moderate–severe serotonin syndrome not settling with supportive care.
Reduces muscle rigidity and heat generation in severe NMS with extreme hyperthermia.
Restores dopaminergic tone in NMS; used adjunctively in severe cases.

decision.label: Stop the agent; aggressive supportive care ± specific antidote

confirm: Hyperthermia, rigidity and altered mental state with autonomic instability — serotonergic excess (clonus, hyperreflexia, rapid onset) vs NMS (lead-pipe rigidity, antipsychotic, slower).
